doc:
A `Scope` records the part of the `CommandElabM` state that respects scoping,
such as the data for `universe`, `open`, and `variable` declarations, the current namespace,
and currently enabled options.
The `CommandElabM` state contains a stack of scopes, and only the top `Scope`
on the stack is read from or modified. There is always at least one `Scope` on the stack,
even outside any `section` or `namespace`, and each new pushed `Scope`
starts as a modified copy of the previous top scope.

fun name default =>
  have name := name.eraseMacroScopes;
  do
  let args ← get
  let __s ←
    forIn' [:args.size] (none, ()) fun i h __s =>
        have __r := __s;
        match Lean.Doc.getFlag.asFlag✝ args[i].raw with
        | some (x, v) =>
          if (x.getId.eraseMacroScopes == name) = true then do
            set
                (↑(args.toSubarray 0 i) ++
                  ↑(have a := args;
                    a.toSubarray (i + 1)))
            pure (ForInStep.done (some v, ()))
          else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
        | x => pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
  have __r : Option Bool × Unit := __s
  match __r.1 with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => pure default

fun initialLctx docState =>
  have pending := #[];
  do
  let __s ←
    forIn docState.lctx pending fun decl __s =>
        have pending := __s;
        if initialLctx.containsFVar (Lean.Expr.fvar decl.fvarId) = true then
          pure (ForInStep.yield pending)
        else do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars decl.type
          let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getMVars __do_lift)
          have pending : Array Lean.MVarId := pending ++ __do_lift
          match decl.value? with
            | some v => do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars v
              let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getMVars __do_lift)
              have pending : Array Lean.MVarId := pending ++ __do_lift
              pure (ForInStep.yield pending)
            | x => pure (ForInStep.yield pending)
  have pending : Array Lean.MVarId := __s
  if pending.isEmpty = true then pure ()
    else discard (Lean.Elab.Term.logUnassignedUsingErrorInfos pending)

fun ref hintTitle newStrings => do
  let __do_lift ← read
  match __do_lift.suggestionMode with
    | Lean.Doc.SuggestionMode.interactive =>
      liftM
        (hintTitle.hint
          (Array.map
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (s, preInfo?, postInfo?) =>
                { suggestion := Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.SuggestionText.string s,
                  preInfo? := preInfo?, postInfo? := postInfo? })
            newStrings)
          (some ref))
    | Lean.Doc.SuggestionMode.batch =>
      match ref.getRange? with
      | some { start := b, stop := e } => do
        let text ← Lean.getFileMap
        have pre : String := String.Pos.Raw.extract text.source 0 b
        have post : String := String.Pos.Raw.extract text.source e text.source.rawEndPos
        have edits : Array Lean.MessageData :=
          Array.map
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (s, fst, snd) =>
                have lines := (text.source.split '\n').toStringArray;
                have s' := pre ++ s ++ post;
                have lines' := (s'.split '\n').toStringArray;
                have d := Lean.Diff.diff lines lines';
                Lean.toMessageData
                  (Lean.Diff.linesToString
                    (Array.filter (fun x => x.1 != Lean.Diff.Action.skip) d)))
            newStrings
        pure
            (Lean.toMessageData "\n\nHint: " ++ Lean.toMessageData hintTitle ++
                Lean.toMessageData "\n" ++
              Lean.toMessageData
                (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.joinSep edits.toList (Lean.toMessageData "\n"))))

doc:
Try to synthesize `mvarId` by starting using a default instance with the given priority.
This method succeeds only if the metavariable of fully synthesized.

Remark: In the past, we would return a list of pending TC problems, but this was problematic since
a default instance may create subproblems that cannot be solved.

Remark: The new approach also has limitations because other pending metavariables are not taken into account
while backtracking. That is, we fail to synthesize `mvarId` because we reach subproblems that are stuck,
but we could "unstuck" them if we tried to solve other pending metavariables. Considering all pending metavariables
into a single backtracking search seems to be too expensive, and potentially generate incomprehensible error messages.
This is particularly true if we consider pending metavariables for "postponed" elaboration steps.
Here is an example that demonstrate this issue. The example considers we are using the old `binrel%` elaborator which was
disconnected from `binop%`.
```
example (a : Int) (b c : Nat) : a = ↑b - ↑c := sorry
```
We have two pending coercions for the `↑` and `HSub ?m.220 ?m.221 ?m.222`.
When we did not use a backtracking search here, then the homogeneous default instance for `HSub`.
```
instance [Sub α] : HSub α α α where
```
would be applied first, and would propagate the expected type `Int` to the pending coercions which would now be unblocked.

Instead of performing a backtracking search that considers all pending metavariables, we improved the `binrel%` elaborator.

doc:
Try to solve postponed universe constraints, and throws an exception if there are stuck constraints.

Remark: in previous versions, each `isDefEq u v` invocation would fail if there
were pending universe level constraints. With this old approach, we were not able
to process
```
Functor.map Prod.fst (x s)
```
because after elaborating `Prod.fst` and trying to ensure its type
match the expected one, we would be stuck at the universe constraint:
```
u =?= max u ?v
```
Another benefit of using `withoutPostponingUniverseConstraints` is better error messages. Instead
of getting a mysterious type mismatch constraint, we get a list of
universe constraints the system is stuck at.

fun ignoreStuckTC => do
  let pendingMVars ←
    modifyGet fun s =>
        (s.pendingMVars,
          { levelNames := s.levelNames, syntheticMVars := s.syntheticMVars, pendingMVars := [],
            mvarErrorInfos := s.mvarErrorInfos, levelMVarErrorInfos := s.levelMVarErrorInfos,
            mvarArgNames := s.mvarArgNames, letRecsToLift := s.letRecsToLift })
  let pendingMVarsWithDecls ←
    List.filterMapM
        (fun mvarId => do
          let __x ← Lean.Elab.Term.getSyntheticMVarDecl? mvarId
          match __x with
            | some decl => pure (some (mvarId, decl))
            | x => pure none)
        pendingMVars
  have prioritizedProblems : List (Lean.MVarId × Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarDecl) :=
    pendingMVarsWithDecls.mergeSort fun x x_1 =>
      match x with
      | (fst, decl1) =>
        match x_1 with
        | (fst, decl2) =>
          match (decl1.kind, decl2.kind) with
          |
          (Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarKind.typeClass extraErrorMsg?,
              Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarKind.typeClass extraErrorMsg?_1) =>
            match (decl1.stx.getRange?, decl2.stx.getRange?) with
            | (some r1, some r2) =>
              if (r1.bsize != r2.bsize) = true then decide (r1.bsize ≤ r2.bsize)
              else decide (r1.start ≤ r2.start)
            | (none, snd) => false
            | x => true
          | (Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarKind.typeClass extraErrorMsg?, snd) => false
          | x => true
  forIn prioritizedProblems PUnit.unit fun x __s =>
      match x with
      | (mvarId, mvarDecl) => do
        Lean.Elab.Term.reportStuckSyntheticMVar mvarId mvarDecl ignoreStuckTC
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
  pure ()

fun mvarId mvarDecl ignoreStuckTC =>
  Lean.withRef mvarDecl.stx
    (match mvarDecl.kind with
    | Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarKind.typeClass extraErrorMsg? =>
      have extraErrorMsg := Lean.Elab.Term.extraMsgToMsg extraErrorMsg?;
      if ignoreStuckTC = true then pure ()
      else
        mvarId.withContext do
          let mvarDecl ← Lean.Elab.Term.getMVarDecl mvarId
          let __do_lift ← Lean.MonadLog.hasErrors
          if __do_lift = true then pure ()
            else do
              let __x ← Lean.Elab.Term.explainStuckTypeclassProblem mvarDecl.type
              match __x with
                | some note =>
                  Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData "typeclass instance problem is stuck" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr mvarDecl.type) ++
                        Lean.toMessageData note ++
                      Lean.toMessageData extraErrorMsg)
                | x =>
                  Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData
                          "typeclass instance problem is stuck, it is often due to metavariables" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr mvarDecl.type) ++
                      Lean.toMessageData extraErrorMsg)
    | Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarKind.coe header expectedType e f? mkErrorMsg? =>
      mvarId.withContext
        (match mkErrorMsg? with
        | some mkErrorMsg => do
          let __do_lift ← liftM (mkErrorMsg mvarId expectedType e)
          Lean.throwError __do_lift
        | x => do
          let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.inferType e)
          let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.Elab.Term.getMVarDecl mvarId
          liftM
              (Lean.Elab.Term.throwTypeMismatchError
                (do
                  let a ← header
                  pure ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) a))
                expectedType __do_lift e f?
                (some
                  (Lean.toMessageData "failed to create type class instance for" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr __do_lift_1.type)))))
    | Lean.Elab.Term.SyntheticMVarKind.tactic tacticCode savedContext kind true =>
      Lean.Elab.Term.withSavedContext savedContext
        (mvarId.withContext do
          let mvarDecl ← Lean.Elab.Term.getMVarDecl mvarId
          Lean.throwError
              (Lean.toMessageData "tactic execution is stuck, goal contains metavariables" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr mvarDecl.type)))
    | x =>
      panicWithPosWithDecl "Lean.Elab.SyntheticMVars" "Lean.Elab.Term.reportStuckSyntheticMVar" 316
        11 "unreachable code has been reached")

fun savedContext stx mvarId postponeOnError =>
  Lean.withRef stx
    (mvarId.withContext do
      let s ← Lean.saveState
      let e ←
        tryCatch
            (do
              let r ←
                Lean.Elab.Term.withSavedContext savedContext do
                    let mvarDecl ← Lean.Elab.Term.getMVarDecl mvarId
                    let expectedType ← Lean.instantiateMVars mvarDecl.type
                    Lean.Elab.withInfoHole mvarId do
                        let result ←
                          Lean.Elab.Term.withTermInfoContext' Lean.Name.anonymous stx do
                              let result ←
                                Lean.Elab.Term.resumeElabTerm✝ stx (some expectedType)
                                    !postponeOnError
                              Lean.withRef stx
                                  (Lean.Elab.Term.ensureHasType (some expectedType) result)
                        let __do_lift ← Lean.occursCheck mvarId result
                        if __do_lift = true then do
                            mvarId.assign result
                            pure true
                          else pure false
              ExceptT.run (pure r))
            fun x =>
            match x with
            | ex@h:(Lean.Exception.internal id extra) =>
              if (id == Lean.Elab.postponeExceptionId) = true then do
                s.restore true
                EarlyReturnT.return false
              else do
                let r ← throw ex
                ExceptT.run (pure r)
            | ex@h:(Lean.Exception.error ref msg) =>
              if postponeOnError = true then do
                s.restore true
                EarlyReturnT.return false
              else do
                Lean.Elab.logException ex
                EarlyReturnT.return true
      EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r)

If `postpone == .no`,then `pendingMVars` is `[]` after executing this method.
If `postpone == .partial`, then `pendingMVars` contains only `.tc` and `.coe` kinds.

It keeps executing `synthesizeSyntheticMVarsStep` while progress is being made.
If `postpone != .yes`, then it applies default instances to `SyntheticMVarKind.typeClass` (if available)
metavariables that are still unresolved, and then tries to resolve metavariables
with `postponeOnError == false`. That is, we force them to produce error messages and/or commit to
a "best option". If, after that, we still haven't made progress, we report "stuck" errors If `postpone == .no`.

pending TC problems become implicit parameters for the simp theorem.

doc:
Update `indices` by including any free variable `x` s.t.
- Type of some `discr` depends on `x`.
- Type of `x` depends on some free variable in `indices`.

If we don't include these extra variables in indices, then
`updateMatchType` will generate a type incorrect term.
For example, suppose `discr` contains `h : @HEq α a α b`, and
`indices` is `#[α, b]`, and `matchType` is `@HEq α a α b → B`.
`updateMatchType indices matchType` produces the type
`(α' : Type) → (b : α') → @HEq α' a α' b → B` which is type incorrect
because we have `a : α`.
The method `collectDeps` will include `a` into `indices`.

This method does not handle dependencies among non-free variables.
We rely on the type checking method `check` at `updateMatchType`.

Remark: `indices : Array Expr` does not need to be an array anymore.
We should cleanup this code, and use `index : Expr` instead.

doc:
This method is part of the "discriminant refinement" procedure. It in invoked when the
type of the `pattern` does not match the expected type. The expected type is based on the
motive computed using the `match` discriminants.
It tries to compute a path to an index of the discriminant type.
For example, suppose the user has written
```
inductive Mem (a : α) : List α → Prop where
  | head {as} : Mem a (a::as)
  | tail {as} : Mem a as → Mem a (a'::as)

infix:50 " ∈ " => Mem

example (a b : Nat) (h : a ∈ [b]) : b = a :=
match h with
| Mem.head => rfl
```
The motive for the match is `a ∈ [b] → b = a`, and get a type mismatch between the type
of `Mem.head` and `a ∈ [b]`. This procedure return the path `[2, 1]` to the index `b`.
We use it to produce the following refinement
```
example (a b : Nat) (h : a ∈ [b]) : b = a :=
match b, h with
| _, Mem.head => rfl
```
which produces the new motive `(x : Nat) →  a ∈ [x] → x = a`
After this refinement step, the `match` is elaborated successfully.

This method relies on the fact that the dependent pattern matcher compiler solves equations
between indices of indexed inductive families.
The following kinds of equations are supported by this compiler:
- `x = t`
- `t = x`
- `ctor ... = ctor ...`

where `x` is a free variable, `t` is an arbitrary term, and `ctor` is constructor.
Our procedure ensures that "information" is not lost, and will *not* succeed in an
example such as
```
example (a b : Nat) (f : Nat → Nat) (h : f a ∈ [f b]) : f b = f a :=
  match h with
  | Mem.head => rfl
```
and will not add `f b` as a new discriminant. We may add an option in the future to
enable this more liberal form of refinement.

We (try to) elaborate a `match` only when the expected type is available.
If the `matchType` has not been provided by the user, we also try to postpone elaboration if the type
of a discriminant is not available. That is, it is of the form `(?m ...)`.
We use `expandNonAtomicDiscrs?` to make sure all discriminants are metavariables,
so that they are not elaborated twice.
This is a standard trick we use in the elaborator, and it is also used to elaborate structure instances.
Suppose, we are trying to elaborate
```
match g x with
  | ... => ...
```
`expandNonAtomicDiscrs?` converts it intro
```
let_mvar% ?discr := g x
match ?discr with
  | ... => ...
```

This elaboration technique is needed to elaborate terms such as:
```lean
xs.filter fun (a, b) => a > b
```
which are syntax sugar for
```lean
List.filter (fun p => match p with | (a, b) => a > b) xs
```
When we visit `match p with | (a, b) => a > b`, we don't know the type of `p` yet.

doc:
"Generalize" variables that depend on the discriminants.

Remarks and limitations:
- We currently do not generalize let-decls.
- We abort generalization if the new `matchType` is type incorrect.
- Only discriminants that are free variables are considered during specialization.
- We "generalize" by adding new discriminants and pattern variables. We do not "clear" the generalized variables,
  but they become inaccessible since they are shadowed by the patterns variables. We assume this is ok since
  this is the exact behavior users would get if they had written it by hand. Recall there is no `clear` in term mode.

value.text:
fun discrs matchType altViews generalizing? =>
  have gen :=
    match generalizing? with
    | some g => g
    | x => true;
  if (!gen) = true then pure { discrs := discrs, matchType := matchType, altViews := altViews }
  else
    have discrExprs := Array.map (fun x => x.expr) discrs;
    do
    let ysFVarIds ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getFVarsToGeneralize discrExprs ∅ true)
    if ysFVarIds.isEmpty = true then
        pure { discrs := discrs, matchType := matchType, altViews := altViews }
      else
        have ys := Array.map Lean.mkFVar ysFVarIds;
        do
        let matchType' ←
          Lean.Meta.forallBoundedTelescope matchType (some discrs.size) fun ds type => do
              let type ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkForallFVars ys type)
              match
                  (Array.filter
                      (fun x =>
                        match x with
                        | (di, snd) => di.isFVar)
                      (discrExprs.zip ds)).unzip with
                | (discrs', ds') =>
                  have type := type.replaceFVars discrs' ds';
                  liftM (Lean.Meta.mkForallFVars ds type)
        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.isTypeCorrect matchType')
        if __do_lift = true then
            have discrs := discrs ++ Array.map (fun y => { expr := y }) ys;
            do
            let altViews ←
              Array.mapM
                  (fun altView => do
                    let patternVars ← Lean.Elab.Term.getPatternsVars altView.patterns
                    let ysUserNames ←
                      Array.foldrM
                          (fun ys ysUserNames => do
                            let yDecl ← liftM ys.fvarId!.getDecl
                            have yUserName : Lean.Name := yDecl.userName
                            have __do_jp :
                              Unit → Lean.Name → Lean.Elab.TermElabM (Array Lean.Name) :=
                              fun __r yUserName => pure (ysUserNames.push yUserName)
                            if ysUserNames.contains yUserName = true then do
                                let yUserName ← liftM (Lean.mkFreshUserName yUserName)
                                __do_jp () yUserName
                              else
                                if
                                    (patternVars.any fun x => Lean.Syntax.getId x == yUserName) =
                                      true then
                                  do
                                  let yUserName ← liftM (Lean.mkFreshUserName yUserName)
                                  __do_jp () yUserName
                                else __do_jp () yUserName)
                          #[] ys
                    let ysIds ←
                      Array.mapM
                          (fun n => do
                            let __do_lift ← Lean.getRef
                            pure (Lean.mkIdentFrom __do_lift n))
                          ysUserNames.reverse
                    pure
                        { ref := altView.ref,
                          patterns := altView.patterns ++ Lean.TSyntaxArray.raw ysIds,
                          lhs := altView.lhs, rhs := altView.rhs })
                  altViews
            pure
                { discrs := discrs, toClear := ysFVarIds, matchType := matchType',
                  altViews := altViews, refined := true }
          else pure { discrs := discrs, matchType := matchType, altViews := altViews }

doc:
Auxiliary function for expanding `fun` notation binders. Recall that `fun` parser is defined as
```
def funBinder : Parser := implicitBinder <|> instBinder <|> termParser maxPrec
leading_parser unicodeSymbol "λ" "fun" >> many1 funBinder >> "=>" >> termParser
```
to allow notation such as `fun (a, b) => a + b`, where `(a, b)` should be treated as a pattern.
The result is a pair `(explicitBinders, newBody)`, where `explicitBinders` is syntax of the form
```
`(` ident `:` term `)`
```
which can be elaborated using `elabBinders`, and `newBody` is the updated `body` syntax.
We update the `body` syntax when expanding the pattern notation.
Example: `fun (a, b) => a + b` expands into `fun _a_1 => match _a_1 with | (a, b) => a + b`.
See local function `processAsPattern` at `expandFunBindersAux`.

The resulting `Bool` is true if a pattern was found. We use it "mark" a macro expansion.

doc:
Expand `matchAlts` syntax into a full `match`-expression.
Example:
```
| 0, true => alt_1
| i, _    => alt_2
```
expands into (for tactic == false)
```
fun x_1 x_2 =>
match @x_1, @x_2 with
| 0, true => alt_1
| i, _    => alt_2
```
and (for tactic == true)
```
intro x_1; intro x_2;
match @x_1, @x_2 with
| 0, true => alt_1
| i, _    => alt_2
```

If `useExplicit = true`, we add a `@` before `fun` to disable implicit lambdas. We disable them when processing `let` and `let rec` declarations
to make sure the behavior is consistent with top-level declarations where we can write
```
def f : {α : Type} → α → α
  | _, a => a
```
We use `useExplicit = false` when we are elaborating the `fun | ... => ... | ...` notation. See issue #1132.
If `@fun` is used with this notation, the we set `useExplicit = true`.
We also use `useExplicit = false` when processing `instance ... where` notation declarations. The motivation is to have compact declarations such as
```
instance [Alternative m] : MonadLiftT Option m where
monadLift -- We don't want to provide the implicit arguments of `monadLift` here. One should use `monadLift := @fun ...` if they want to provide them.
  | some a => pure a
  | none => failure
```

Remark: we add `@` at discriminants to make sure we don't consume implicit arguments, and to make the behavior consistent with `fun`.
Example:
```
inductive T : Type 1 :=
| mkT : (forall {a : Type}, a -> a) -> T

def makeT (f : forall {a : Type}, a -> a) : T :=
  mkT f

def makeT' : (forall {a : Type}, a -> a) -> T
| f => mkT f
```
The two definitions should be elaborated without errors and be equivalent.

doc:
The dependent arrow. `(x : α) → β` is equivalent to `∀ x : α, β`, but we usually
reserve the latter for propositions. Also written as `Π x : α, β` (the "Pi-type")
in the literature.

Sanity-checks the number of patterns in each alternative of a definition by pattern matching.
Specifically, verifies that all alternatives have the same number of patterns and that the number
of patterns is upper-bounded by the number of (dependent) arrows in the expected type.

Note: This function assumes that the number of patterns in the first alternative will be equal to
`numDiscrs` (since we use the first alternative to infer the arity of the generated matcher in
`getMatchAltsNumPatterns`).

  (expectedType : Lean.Expr) : Lean.MetaM Unit

value.text:
fun matchAlts numDiscrs expectedType =>
  have sepPats := fun pats =>
    Lean.MessageData.joinSep (List.map Lean.toMessageData pats)
      ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) ", ");
  do
  let maxDiscrs? ←
    Lean.Meta.forallTelescopeReducing expectedType fun xs e =>
        if e.getAppFn.isMVar = true then pure none else pure (some xs.size)
  have matchAltViews : Array (Lean.Elab.Term.MatchAltView [`term]) :=
    Array.filterMap (Lean.Elab.Term.getMatchAlt [`term]) matchAlts[0].getArgs
  have numPatternsStr : ℕ → String := fun n =>
    toString n ++ toString " " ++ toString (if (n == 1) = true then "pattern" else "patterns")
  if h : matchAltViews.size > 0 then
      have __do_jp := fun __r => do
        forIn matchAltViews PUnit.unit fun view __s =>
            have numPats := view.patterns.size;
            if (numPats != numDiscrs) = true then
              have origPats := sepPats matchAltViews[0].patterns.toList;
              have pats := sepPats view.patterns.toList;
              do
              Lean.throwErrorAt view.lhs
                  (Lean.toMessageData
                                  "Inconsistent number of patterns in match alternatives: This alternative contains " ++
                                Lean.toMessageData (numPatternsStr numPats) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData ":" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD pats) ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "\nbut a preceding alternative contains " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData numDiscrs ++
                      Lean.toMessageData ":" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD origPats))
              pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
            else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        pure ();
      match maxDiscrs? with
      | some maxDiscrs =>
        if numDiscrs > maxDiscrs then
          if (maxDiscrs == 0) = true then do
            let __r ←
              Lean.throwErrorAt matchAltViews[0].lhs
                  (Lean.toMessageData "Cannot define a value of type" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr expectedType) ++
                    Lean.toMessageData "\nby pattern matching because it is not a function type")
            __do_jp __r
          else do
            let __r ←
              Lean.throwErrorAt matchAltViews[0].lhs
                  (Lean.toMessageData "Too many patterns in match alternative: At most " ++
                                Lean.toMessageData (numPatternsStr maxDiscrs) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData " expected in a definition of type " ++
                            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr expectedType) ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "\nbut found " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData numDiscrs ++
                      Lean.toMessageData ":" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (sepPats matchAltViews[0].patterns.toList)))
            __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()
      | x => __do_jp ()
    else pure ()

Position information provider for the Info Tree.
We currently do not track binder "macro expansion" steps in the info tree.
For example, suppose we expand a `_` into a fresh identifier. The fresh identifier
has synthetic position since it was not written by the user, and we would not get
hover information for the `_` because we also don't have this macro expansion step
stored in the info tree. Thus, we store the original `Syntax` in `ref`, and use
it when storing the binder information in the info tree.

Potential better solution: add a binder syntax category, an extensible `elabBinder`
(like we have `elabTerm`), and perform all macro expansion steps at `elabBinder` and
record them in the info tree.

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadOptions m] [Lean.MonadError m] [MonadLiftT (EIO Lean.Exception) m]
    [Lean.Elab.MonadInfoTree m] id val =>
  do
  let ref ← Lean.getRef
  Lean.Elab.addCompletionInfo
      (Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.option (ref.setArgs ↑(Std.Rio.Sliceable.mkSlice ref.getArgs *...3)))
  have optionName : Lean.Name := id.getId.eraseMacroScopes
  let decl ←
    liftM
        (IO.toEIO
          (fun ex =>
            Lean.Exception.error ref ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) ex.toString))
          (Lean.getOptionDecl optionName))
  Lean.Elab.pushInfoLeaf
      (Lean.Elab.Info.ofOptionInfo
        { stx := id, optionName := optionName, declName := decl.declName })
  match val.isStrLit? with
    | some str => Lean.Elab.elabSetOption.setOption✝ optionName decl (Lean.DataValue.ofString str)
    | none =>
      match val.isNatLit? with
      | some num => Lean.Elab.elabSetOption.setOption✝ optionName decl (Lean.DataValue.ofNat num)
      | none =>
        match val with
        | Lean.Syntax.atom info "true" =>
          Lean.Elab.elabSetOption.setOption✝ optionName decl (Lean.DataValue.ofBool true)
        | Lean.Syntax.atom info "false" =>
          Lean.Elab.elabSetOption.setOption✝ optionName decl (Lean.DataValue.ofBool false)

                    Lean.toMessageData "`; expected a literal of type `" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData ctorType ++
                Lean.toMessageData "`")

The action is run in a context with an empty message log, empty trace state, and empty info trees.

doc:
If `hint?` is `some hint`, establishes a new context for macro scope naming and runs `act` in it,
otherwise runs `act` directly without changes.

Context names as documented in Note `Macro Scope Representation` help with avoiding rebuilds and
`prefer_native` lookup misses from macro scopes in declaration names and other exported information.
This function establishes a new context with a globally unique name by combining the name of the
current module with `hint` while also checking for previously used `hint`s in the same module.
Thus `hint` does not need to be unique but ensuring it is usually unique helps with keeping the
context name stable.

In the current implementation, we call `withInitQuotContext` once in `elabCommandTopLevel` using the
source input of the command as the hint. This helps with keeping macro scopes stable on changes to
other parts of the file but not on changes to the command itself. Thus in each *declaration*
elaborator we call `withInitQuotContext` again with the declaration name(s) as a hint so that
changes to any other part of the declaration do not change the context name.

Note that `x` is executed with an empty message log. Thus, `x` cannot modify/view messages produced by

#eval

Produces an iterator that emits one value of `it`, then drops `n - 1` elements, then emits another
value, and so on. In other words, it emits every `n`-th value of `it`, starting with the first one.

If `n = 0`, the iterator behaves like for `n = 1`: It emits all values of `it`.


**Marble diagram:**

```
it               ---1----2----3---4----5
it.stepSize 2    ---1---------3--------5
```

**Availability:**

This operation is currently only available for iterators implementing `IteratorAccess`,
such as `PRange.iter` range iterators.

**Termination properties:**

* `Finite` instance: only if the base iterator `it` is finite
* `Productive` instance: always

doc:
Recall that `mkTermInfo` does not create an `ofTermInfo` node in the info tree
if `e` corresponds to a hole that is going to be filled "later" by executing a tactic or resuming elaboration.
This behavior is problematic for auxiliary elaboration steps that are "almost" no-ops.
For example, consider the elaborator for
```
ensure_type_of% s msg e
```
It elaborates `s`, infers its type `t`, and then elaborates `e` ensuring the resulting type is `t`.
If the elaboration of `e` is postponed, then the result is just a metavariable, and an `ofTermInfo` would not be created.
This happens because `ensure_type_of%` is almost a no-op. The elaboration of `s` does not directly contribute to the
final result, just its type.
To make sure, we don't miss any information in the `InfoTree`, we can just create a "silent" annotation to force
`mTermInfo` to create a node for the `ensure_type_of% s msg e` even if `e` has been postponed.

Another possible solution is to elaborate `ensure_type_of% s msg e` as `ensureType s e` where `ensureType` has type
```
ensureType (s e : α) := e
```
We decided to use the silent notation because `ensure_type_of%` is heavily used in the `Do` elaborator, and the extra
overhead could be significant.

doc:
Instructs the compiler to use a different function as the implementation of a function. With the
exception of tactics that call native code such as `native_decide`, the kernel and type checking
are unaffected. When this attribute is used on a function, the function is not compiled and all
compiler-related attributes (e.g. `noncomputable`, `@[inline]`) are ignored. Calls to this
function are replaced by calls to its implementation.

The most common use cases of `@[implemented_by]` are to provide an efficient unsafe implementation
and to make an unsafe function accessible in safe code through an opaque function:

```
unsafe def testEqImpl (as bs : Array Nat) : Bool :=
  ptrEq as bs || as == bs

@[implemented_by testEqImpl]
def testEq (as bs : Array Nat) : Bool :=
  as == bs

unsafe def printAddrImpl {α : Type u} (x : α) : IO Unit :=
  IO.println s!"Address: {ptrAddrUnsafe x}"

@[implemented_by printAddrImpl]
opaque printAddr {α : Type u} (x : α) : IO Unit
```

The provided implementation is not checked to be equivalent to the original definition. This makes
it possible to prove `False` with `native_decide` using incorrect implementations. For a safer
variant of this attribute that however doesn't work for unsafe implementations, see `@[csimp]`,
which requires a proof that the two functions are equal.

fun h nBytes expectedMethod α [Lean.FromJson α] => do
  let m ← h.readMessage nBytes
  match m with
    | Lean.JsonRpc.Message.notification method params? =>
      if method = expectedMethod then
        have j := Lean.toJson params?;
        match Lean.fromJson? j with
        | Except.ok v => pure { method := expectedMethod, param := v }
        | Except.error inner =>
          throw
            (IO.userError
              (toString "Unexpected param '" ++ toString j.compress ++ toString "' for method '" ++
                    toString expectedMethod ++
                  toString "'\n" ++
                toString inner))
      else
        throw
          (IO.userError
            (toString "Expected method '" ++ toString expectedMethod ++
                  toString "', got method '" ++
                toString method ++
              toString "'"))
    | x =>
